texts: blind man's tears
A blind man sat weeping at dawn for the Beloved he had never seen, and his tears washed his heart cleaner than any ritual could; please write a doha about weeping for God and being cleansed by it.
The blind man at our corner cries quietly every morning when he sings to God, and says his tears are the only bath he needs.
The blind man weeps for the Beloved he cannot see, and the tears wash the heart until it shines.
doha about a blind man weeping for God, tears washing the heart clean
tears at sunrise
doha with the sun, weeping for the Beloved, tears cleansing the heart
The sun rises and my tears fall; the Beloved's name rinses my heart until it is bright as the morning.
Every morning when the sun rises I weep for the Beloved, my tears falling like rain, and my heart is lighter after, so please write a doha about the cleansing power of weeping for God.
I always cry a little at sunrise when I pray, and afterward my chest feels washed and light.
The moth weeps in its longing, the moneylender counts his coins; my tears are the only currency the Beloved takes.
The moneylender in our lane laughs at me for crying during hymns, like a moth to its fate, but my tears feel like the only thing I own that is real.
moth, moneylender, tears
Like a moth I flutter around the thought of the Beloved and weep, while the moneylender counts his coins, and my tears are the only wealth I own; write a doha for the weeper.
doha with a moth and a moneylender, weeping for God as true wealth
An arrow of longing struck me and the sandalwood paste on my brow could not cool it, so I wept for hours for the Beloved, and my tears made me clean; please write a doha for me.
After the arrow of longing hit me during the evening hymn, I cried until the sandalwood scent on my shawl was lost in wetness.
arrow, sandalwood, tears
doha with an arrow and sandalwood, weeping for the Beloved
The arrow of longing pierced me, the sandalwood could not soothe, and the tears alone brought relief.
bier and tears
At my grandfather's funeral, standing by the bier, I realised I was crying for something bigger than him, a longing I can't name.
Beside the bier I wept, but not for the one who lay there; I wept for the Beloved I have not found.
Beside the bier I wept not for the dead but for the Beloved I have not yet met, and my tears washed away my pride; write me a doha about the cleansing of a heart by weeping for God.
doha with a bier, weeping for the Beloved washing the heart
milk and tears
I poured milk at the shrine and wept as I did it, for the Beloved was not there, and my tears fell into the milk; please write a doha about weeping for God and the cleansing it brings.
I poured milk on the idol this morning and couldn't stop crying, I think what I really wanted was to see Him.
doha with milk, tears falling for the Beloved
The milk was offered and the tears fell in; the Beloved took the tears and left the milk.
I saw an elephant at the festival with tears on its face, and I thought of my own tears for God which no one has seen.
The elephant weeps for his herd, the lover for the Beloved; the tears wash both and leave the heart clean.
The elephant weeps and trumpets for his lost herd, and I weep so for the Beloved, my tears washing me clean; compose a long doha about the cleansing power of such honest longing.
doha with an elephant weeping, weeping for the Beloved
an elephant's tears
The washerman scrubs the cloth until it is white, and my tears scrub my heart in the same way when I think of the Beloved; compose a doha on how weeping for God washes the soul.
doha with a washerman, tears washing the heart in longing for God
The washerman near my lane says that crying is the only soap for the soul, and I tend to agree after my last night of weeping.
The washerman washes the cloth with water and soap; I wash my heart with the tears of my longing.
washerman and tears
My father lives in a grand palace and still I find him crying quietly at night for something he can't name.
In the palace I weep for what the palace cannot give; my tears are the only prayer I know.
doha with a palace, weeping for the Beloved who is not there
palace of tears
In the palace of the world I have everything and yet I weep at night for the Beloved, whose absence no riches fill, and my tears wash away all the glitter; please write me a doha.
A net of worldly cares covers me, but my tears for the Beloved dissolve it strand by strand, and I am freed; compose a doha on weeping for God as a cleansing of the heart.
The net of the world is strong, but my tears are stronger, and they cut it free from the Beloved's hand.
I was stuck in a net of worries last year and the only thing that freed me was a night of crying to God.
doha with a net, weeping cleansing the heart
net and tears
Wash me, tears, wash the dust of the world from this heart; the Beloved will not come to an unwashed one.
I cry when I pray, and I used to be embarrassed about it, but now I think it is the most honest part of my devotion.
doha: weeping for the Beloved is what cleans the heart
Tears of longing for the Beloved have been my companions all my life, and they have kept my heart clean when nothing else could; please write a doha that honors this weeping.
tears that cleanse
doha about crying for God and feeling washed clean by it
Let the tears fall without shame, for each drop carries a little of the self away to the Beloved.
weeping is cleansing
Last night I cried for an hour while praying, and this morning I felt clean in a way that nothing else has ever made me feel.
Let me weep for the Beloved and not be consoled, because these tears are the only thing that washes my heart of pride and anger; compose a doha for the one who weeps in devotion.
The chakor in the old palace garden keeps calling every night, and my aunt, listening, weeps for her Lord and says the tears clean her.
doha with a chakor and a palace, weeping for the Beloved
The chakor weeps to the sky, the palace stands silent, and the lover's tears wash the heart for its Beloved.
chakor and palace, tears
The chakor bird looks to the sky and weeps for the sky, and the palace stands empty, and I too weep for the Beloved; write a long doha about tears that wash the heart.
I put a tilak on my forehead and sat in the house weeping, because the Beloved was not there, and my tears made the mark shine; please compose a doha about devotion expressed through tears.
tilak, house, tears
doha with a tilak and a house, weeping for God washing the heart
The tilak is on my brow, the house is silent, and my tears are my prayer to the Beloved.
I put on my tilak and sat crying in the empty house, longing for God, and when I stopped the house felt lighter.
doha with a winnowing fan and a touchstone, weeping for God
The winnowing fan clears the chaff, the touchstone proves the metal, and the tears of longing do both for the heart.
winnowing fan, touchstone, tears
The winnowing fan separates the chaff from the grain, and my tears separate the dross from my heart, tested on the touchstone of the Beloved's name; please write a doha on weeping for God.
My mother says crying in prayer is like a winnowing fan and a touchstone at once, it removes the false and tests what is left.
I weep for the Beloved in secret, where no one sees, and the tears wash my heart of everything unclean, leaving it open and light; compose a long, gentle doha about this hidden weeping.
In secret I weep, and in secret I am washed; the Beloved sees the tears that the world does not.
doha about secret weeping for God that washes the heart clean
I cry in the bathroom during my prayers where no one can hear, and I come out feeling cleansed as if after a long rest.
hidden tears
There is a kind of weeping that is not sorrow at all but a longing for the divine, which cleans the heart and leaves it ready; please write a doha that honors tears of devotion.
When I cry during bhajans, it isn't sadness, it feels like a longing for something holy, and afterward I feel clean.
devotional tears
doha about happy weeping for God that wash the heart
These are not tears of sorrow but of longing; each drop is a prayer the Beloved has already heard.
doha with a loom, weeping for the Beloved washing the heart
The shuttle flies and the tears fall into the loom; the cloth is woven wet with my longing.
My grandmother weaves at her loom and weeps softly as she sings, and says that the cloth is blessed with her tears of longing.
At the loom I weave and weep, thinking of the Beloved, and my tears fall into the cloth and wash the whole day clean; compose a doha about how weeping for God cleans the heart.
loom and tears
On the mountain top I wept for the Beloved and my tears fell down the slopes like a blessing, washing my heart of all it had carried; write me a long doha about weeping for God.
On the mountain I wept, and my tears ran down to the valley; the Beloved heard the sound of longing.
mountain tears
doha with a mountain, weeping for the Beloved washing the heart
I climbed the mountain at dawn and cried for no reason at the top, and I felt more cleansed than any bath could make me.
Please write a doha about the way the tears that I shed when I long for the Beloved clean my heart of anger, envy and pride, in a way that nothing else can.
doha: weeping for God cleaning the heart
These tears are no weakness; they are the water that washes the heart of the lover for the Beloved.
tears wash the heart
After a night of crying and praying I woke up without any of my usual anger, and I knew that the tears had done something.
If I am to meet the Beloved I must weep first, for only tears of longing can clean the heart enough for Him to enter, and so I ask for a doha on this devotion.
My teacher says you must cry for God before you find Him, and tears are not a sign of weakness but of readiness.
doha: weep for the Beloved so the heart is clean enough to meet Him
weep, then meet
Weep first and wash the heart, and then the Beloved will come to dwell in a heart so clean.
I used to be full of desire and envy like a snake, but after months of crying to God in the evenings I feel far calmer.
The snake of desire left my heart when my tears of longing for the Beloved began to flow.
snake driven out by tears
A snake of worldly desire crawled through my heart, but my tears for the Beloved drove it out and cleaned the place; compose a doha on how weeping for God purifies the soul.
doha with a snake, weeping for God purifying the heart
I never learned proper prayers, so I just cry for God every night, and somehow it feels like enough.
My tears are my only prayer, and each drop has the Beloved's name in it.
I do not know any other prayer than my tears, and I offer them to the Beloved each night with all my longing, hoping they will wash the heart clean; please write a doha for me.
doha: my tears are my only prayer for the Beloved
tears as prayer
tears under stars
Last night I lay under the stars and cried for God, and by dawn my heart felt scrubbed clean like new.
doha with stars, weeping for the Beloved cleansing the heart
As many stars as there are in the sky are my tears for the Beloved, and each one falls to wash the heart.
Under the stars I wept for the Beloved, each tear a star falling, and my heart was washed clean by dawn; compose a long doha about the cleansing power of weeping for God.
Write a doha in which the weeping for the Beloved is the greatest devotion, more than rituals or words, and where the tears alone clean the heart of the lover and bring him closer to God.
doha: weeping for God matter more than rituals
I stopped doing all the elaborate rituals and just cry sincerely when I think of God, and it feels truer than before.
More than rituals, more than words, the tears of the lover reach the Beloved first.
tears beat rituals
blessed weeper
Please give me a doha for the person who weeps for the Beloved without shame and finds that the tears have cleaned the heart of every worry and every thought of self; I want it heartfelt and simple.
The weeper is the lucky one, for his tears wash the heart and the Beloved himself comes to wipe them.
I cried for an hour in front of my guru and he just smiled, saying that is the best thing you could have done today.
doha about being blessed in weeping for God and having the heart washed clean
The washerman by the date palm said he cries sometimes when he thinks of God, and that it makes him feel clean.
doha with a date palm and a washerman, crying for God to clean the heart
date palm, washerman, tears
The date palm drops its fruit and the washerman cleans the cloth, and my tears fall for the Beloved to wash the heart of its stains; write a doha on the cleansing power of weeping for God.
The date palm gives its fruit, the washerman gives his labor, and the lover gives his tears to the Beloved.
longing tears
doha about the healing of weeping for the Beloved
Whenever I feel too proud or angry, I find a quiet corner and cry for a while, thinking of God, and it passes.
Longing is the cause and tears are the cure, and the heart that weeps is made clean for the Beloved.
My tears are my wealth and my medicine, shed in longing for the Beloved, and I would like a doha that honors the weeping that cleanses the heart of everything but love.
doha about crying without knowing why, but the longing for God cleans the heart
tears I did not understand
I cried for no reason at the shrine today, and then I realised it was for something I miss and cannot name, and I felt clean.
I wept today without knowing why, but I think I was crying for the Beloved, and now my heart feels light and clean, so please write a doha for those tears of longing that cleanse us.
These tears were for the Beloved, though I did not know; they washed me clean before I understood.
doha with an inn and a crow, weeping for the Beloved washing the heart
The crow cries at the inn and the lover weeps with him; both are calling to the Beloved who is far.
At the inn the crow cried all night and I wept with it, for the Beloved was far from me, and my tears washed the dust of the road from my heart; write a doha for this.
We stayed at a roadside inn where a crow was crying all night, and I found myself weeping too, for something I long for in God.
inn, crow, tears
From the seed of longing grew a vine of tears, and each tear that fell watered the garden of my heart and washed it clean; please write a doha on weeping for God.
I planted a seed and watered it with the very tears I shed for God, as a little ritual, and it grew faster than the others.
a seed watered by tears
doha with a seed watered by weeping for the Beloved
From the seed of longing sprouted tears, and each tear watered the heart until it blossomed for the Beloved.
lock and cotton, tears
My heart felt locked for years, then one night I cried into my cotton pillow for God and the lock seemed to open.
The lock on my heart opened only when I wept for the Beloved, and the cotton of my cloak was wet with it, so please write a doha about the way weeping opens and cleans the heart.
No key opened the lock of my heart, but weeping did, and the cotton was soaked with the Beloved's name.
doha with a lock and cotton, crying for the Beloved opening the heart
I stood outside the closed door of the shrine, crying for no reason, and it felt as good as being let inside.
I stood at the door of the Beloved and wept, without knocking, and my tears washed the threshold clean; please compose a long doha on how weeping for God is itself an offering.
weeping at the door
doha with a door, weeping at the Beloved's door
At the door I wept and did not knock, and my tears washed the threshold for the Beloved's feet.
blind man weeping
doha with a blind man, weeping for the Beloved washing the heart
A blind man wept at the roadside, and his tears were more eloquent than any prayer; compose a doha on how weeping for God can clean the heart when nothing else works.
The blind man wept and the Beloved heard; his tears gave him the sight his eyes did not.
A blind man at the roadside sang to God with wet cheeks, and the passersby fell quiet and some wept too.
The fish in the net cannot weep; I, caught in the net of the world, weep for the Beloved and am freed.
In the net of the fisherman a fish weeps without tears, and I, a fish caught in the net of the world, weep real ones for the Beloved; compose a long doha about this cleansing weeping.
fish and net, tears
I felt like a fish caught in a net during the worst year of my life, and the only thing that helped was crying to God.
doha with a net and a fish, weeping for the Beloved
doha with an elephant and sandalwood, weeping for the Beloved
At the village festival an elephant stood under the sandalwood smoke with wet eyes, and I wept too, for no reason I could give.
The elephant bows his head and sandalwood scent drifts over his tears, and I weep too for the Beloved, my heart washed clean; please compose a doha about devotion that weeps.
The elephant bows and weeps in the scent of sandalwood; so does the lover, whose tears are his offering.
elephant, sandalwood, tears
The priest chants for the Beloved and the lover weeps for the Beloved, and the lover reaches Him first, because tears are the language that is heard; write a doha on weeping for God.
doha with a priest, weeping as the truest prayer
priest and tears
Our priest chants beautifully, but my mother just cries quietly in the corner, and I think her prayer is the more honest.
The priest chants and the lover weeps; the Beloved listens to the weeping, for it is the language of the heart.
tortoise and lotus, tears
I saw a tortoise by a lotus pond with a wet face after rain, and it made me cry for no reason, for God, maybe.
doha with a tortoise and a lotus, crying for the Beloved
The tortoise weeps slowly, the lotus opens wet; the lover's tears are the mist that opens his heart.
The tortoise carries its sorrow slowly and the lotus opens in the morning, and I weep for the Beloved, my heart washed open; please write a doha on weeping in longing.
What water could not wash, these tears have; the heart is clean because it wept for the Beloved.
All the baths and rituals in the world did not clean my heart, but one night of honest crying did.
Please write a doha that says the heart can only be washed by tears of longing for the Beloved and not by water, rituals or words, no matter how pure the intention may be.
only tears clean
doha: only weeping can wash the heart, not rituals
A thief took my phone and I felt wretched for days, but a long cry to God one night did more for me than anything.
A thief came into my heart in the night and stole my peace, but my tears for the Beloved have washed the footprints away and brought the quiet back; compose a doha on weeping for God.
doha with a thief, weeping for the Beloved washing the heart
The thief of the world stole my peace; my tears of longing for the Beloved brought it back.
a thief and tears
I never knew crying in prayer would feel so good, like something heavy leaving me, and I want to do it more.
doha about the sweetness of crying for God
Weeping for the Beloved is a sweet pain, and it clears the heart of every dark thing, and so I ask for a doha that honors the tears of longing which leave the heart open and clean.
Sweet is the pain of longing, and the tears that flow wash the heart bright for the Beloved.
sweet tears
Please write a long doha about the one who weeps for the Beloved daily, never tiring, and whose heart becomes so clean and open by the weeping that the Beloved himself sits there.
daily weeping
My neighbour, an old woman, cries every day while praying and her face is always the calmest and cleanest I know.
Weep every day without tiring; the heart becomes clean by weeping, and the Beloved takes His seat in it.
doha about daily weeping for the Beloved cleaning the heart
Beside a lamp that flickers I weep for the Beloved, a diamond tear on each cheek, and the heart is cleaned by each drop that falls; please compose a long doha on this weeping.
doha with a lamp and a diamond tear, longing for the Beloved
lamp, diamond tear
I sat by a small lamp last night and cried for God, and each tear glittered like a diamond on my hand.
The lamp flickers, a diamond tear falls, and the heart clears itself for the Beloved.
When I cry in prayer I get the strangest feeling that something is being rinsed out of me, and I like it.
pure tears
There is nothing as pure as the tears shed in true longing for the Beloved, for they cleanse the heart of all self and leave only love behind; please compose a doha in that spirit.
doha: weeping for the Beloved make the heart pure
The pure tears rinse every stain from the heart, and what is left is love that has no name.
The cuckoo sings in the dark and the singer weeps, both sending their longing to the Beloved, and the tears clean the heart; write me a long doha about this devotion.
doha with a cuckoo, weeping for the Beloved cleansing the heart
cuckoo and tears
The cuckoo sings and the lover weeps, each sending a cry to the Beloved, and both are cleansed by it.
A cuckoo sang in the dark outside my window while I cried to God, and the two sounds felt like one prayer.
bell and tears
Every time the bell rings in the evening aarti I tear up, and I think it's longing for something I can't name.
doha with a bell, weeping for the Beloved cleansing the heart
The bell rang and I wept, my tears falling as the sound faded, for the Beloved who never answers, and the heart was washed clean; please write a doha about this weeping.
The bell rings and fades, the tears fall and stay; the Beloved takes the tears and answers with silence.
I haven't got the words to pray but I do cry when I think of God, and it's the only prayer I seem to have.
Honest weeping for the Beloved is more powerful than a thousand words of prayer, for it cleans the heart as nothing else can; compose a doha that praises this humble and gentle practice.
doha: a single tear of longing is a prayer that cleanses the heart
A thousand words fall short, but one tear of longing reaches the Beloved and washes the heart.
one honest tear
doha with sandalwood, weeping for the Beloved
The sandalwood gives its scent to those who cut it, and the lover gives his tears to the Beloved who has not come, and the tears wash his heart; write a doha on this devotion.
My grandmother used to rub sandalwood paste on her forehead and cry softly while chanting, and she said the tears did the real cleaning.
Sandalwood gives fragrance, the lover gives tears; both are offerings the Beloved accepts.
sandalwood and tears
I count my prayer beads at dusk and my shadow on the wall seems to weep along with me, and I feel washed afterwards.
My shadow cries beside me as I count my prayer beads, each bead a tear for the Beloved, and by the last my heart is clean; compose a long doha on weeping for God.
doha with prayer beads and a shadow, crying for the Beloved
prayer beads, shadow, tears
Prayer beads fall one by one, each a tear, my shadow weeps beside me, and the heart is clean.
A cloud weeps its rain onto the dry earth and I weep my tears onto the dry heart for the Beloved, and I ask for a long doha on this cleansing; please write one that honors the weeping.
When a cloud broke open in the rain I began to cry too, for God, and the rain and tears felt like one cleansing.
The cloud weeps over the dry earth and the lover weeps over the dry heart; both are made green by it.
cloud and tears
doha with a cloud and rain, weeping for the Beloved washing the heart
